conclusions: The harshness/center-bias report is plausibly a selection artifact as much as a synthesis artifact: the 60-second prime is chosen by a scalar score that contains no stereo-width or harshness term, so a center-heavy, bright interval can be selected even if the full 600-second render is not uniformly centered (context_packet.md:31-35; main.rs:8141-8145, 8463-8479).

The renderer's stereo path is structurally biased toward high L/R correlation: side is derived from L-R, then scaled by a bounded learned width (0.05..0.50) and a bounded side gain, and the mid/side recombination plus bounded pan cannot synthesize side information that the pre-mid/side signal lacks (main.rs:5565-5603; stereo.rs:5-11, 28-41).

The pan head is at its +0.10 rail in the latest trace (deepseek_packet.md:39), and pan_center_loss penalizes only the bounded residual pan (stereo.rs:21-26), so the loss does not directly reward correlation=1; the observed correlation is more consistent with a collapsed side path than with pan alone.

The training objective explicitly rewards matching target side/mid, correlation, and level (main.rs:7211-7234), but the learned width control is capped at 0.50 (stereo.rs:6, 28-41) and the side gain is capped (stereo.rs:9-11), so the optimizer cannot close a large target-side gap by widening alone; it can instead reduce correlation by other means or accept the gap.

The prompt file is written after rendering and prime extraction (main.rs:8682-8697), so its descriptive words ('focused center image', 'bright glassy upper spectrum') cannot have caused the current run's audio; they are post-hoc descriptions (context_packet.md:19-21).

The waveform-filter / diffusion framing is a category error for this codebase: forward has no target-audio argument (context_packet.md:13-15; AUDIO_SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENTATION_PLAN.md:101), and offline waveform filtering is not a proxy for latent-field diffusion (context_packet.md:64-67).

Several loss terms are computed on detached targets and on tanh'd audio (main.rs:7103-7111, 7144-7176), which is correct for target detachment but means the 'harshness' seen post-master is only partially represented in the differentiable objective; the post path adds tanh saturation, a DC blocker, and whole-file peak normalization (main.rs:8059-8076, 8451-8514).

The prime selection score (field_entropy * activity_health + structured_complexity * 0.75 - stagnation * 0.25) is a within-run argmax over a sliding window (main.rs:8141-8145, 8463-8479); it can amplify a within-run outlier and has no listener rating or stereo/harshness ranking (context_packet.md:51-53).

The latest lineage is a sequential continuation, not independent seeds or matched arms (context_packet.md:28-29), so comparisons between the untagged parent and tagged continuations confound optimizer state, world state, and target mix.
evidence: Prime selection: main.rs:8141-8145 defines chunk_scores; main.rs:8463-8479 selects best_start by max sliding-window sum; main.rs:8480-8482 maps to frames and applies a 2048-sample fade. No stereo or harshness term appears.

Stereo path: main.rs:5565-5572 computes mid and side from audio_l/audio_r with learned scalars; main.rs:5591-5603 applies width_val and learned_width to side, then a 16-sample Haas delay, then recombines. stereo.rs:5-11 bounds width and side gain; stereo.rs:28-41 bounds learned width to 0.05..0.50.

Pan: stereo.rs:3 sets GLOBAL_PAN_LIMIT=0.10; stereo.rs:13-19 soft_global_pan; stereo.rs:21-26 pan_center_loss penalizes pan.sqr() only. deepseek_packet.md:39 reports global pan 0.0999 at its +0.10 limit.

Losses: main.rs:7103-7111 tanh and target detach; main.rs:7144-7176 mimic/band/chroma/envelope; main.rs:7185-7226 recurrence, modulation, low-band, stereo geometry; main.rs:7227-7234 stereo_balance_loss weights (0.30 side, 0.95 correlation, 0.45 level); main.rs:7245-7256 mimic_loss assembly.
Post path: main.rs:8059-8076 tanh(0.92*x) and stateful DC blocker; main.rs:8451-8454 peak normalization to 0.891; main.rs:8508-8531 PCM16 write and prime fade.
Prompt timing: main.rs:8682-8697 formats and writes suno_priming_prompt after rendering; context_packet.md:19-21 states it is written after rendering and prime extraction.

Forward inputs: context_packet.md:13-15 and AUDIO_SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENTATION_PLAN.md:101 state forward has no target-audio argument; target sampling occurs after forward (main.rs:7041-7054 then 7107).
Lineage: context_packet.md:28-29 states the three latest WAVs form one sequential continuation lineage, not independent seeds or matched arms.

Metrics caveat: METRICS.md:64-76 and context_packet.md:54-57 warn that spectral fractions can reflect denominator or stereo changes and that correlation/side-mid describe stereo, not musical usefulness.
proposed_experiments: Paired-interval prime audit (no training, no renderer change): for the existing latest WAV, compute per-60-second-interval L/R correlation, side/mid dB, and 2-6 kHz / 6-20 kHz fractions; compare the selected prime interval against the full-file distribution. This tests whether the report is a selection artifact. Cite main.rs:8463-8479 for the selection rule.

Frozen side-path probe (no weight change): render a short segment with the existing checkpoint, then offline apply a controlled side-gain multiplier to the pre-master signal and re-master with the same tanh/DC/peak chain (main.rs:8059-8076, 8451-8514). Measure correlation and side/mid. This tests whether the center bias is recoverable by side gain alone or requires new side information.

Loss-gradient attribution (frozen, single chunk): instrument the stereo_balance_loss components (main.rs:7219-7234) on a fixed chunk and report per-component gradient norms to the width head, pan head, and side excitation controls. This tests which term is actually driving the observed correlation.

Target-mix control: hold the model and world state fixed, vary only the target episode selection (main.rs:7107-7140) across a small set of frozen chunks, and measure output correlation and band fractions. This tests whether the center bias tracks the target mix.

Prime-selection counterfactual: recompute the prime window using an alternative score that includes a stereo-width term, and compare the selected interval to the current one. This tests whether the current score systematically prefers center-heavy intervals.

Post-path ablation (offline, copied WAVs only): apply the tanh/DC/peak chain with and without the tanh stage to the same pre-master signal and measure 2-6 kHz / 6-20 kHz fractions. This tests whether the post path contributes to the reported harshness. Do not modify canonical files (context_packet.md:68-70).
uncertainties: Whether the audible harshness is dominated by the renderer's high-band content (scan partials, wavefolder, FM) or by the post-master tanh/DC/peak-normalization chain is not separable from the supplied evidence; the trace's ultrasonic_ratio is a pre-master guardrail, not a harshness score (deepseek_packet.md:40-41; METRICS.md:94-95).

The exact contribution of the target mix to the latest continuation's correlation is unknown; target mix and online learning confound comparisons between elapsed portions of a run (context_packet.md:37-39).

Whether the 60-second prime's center-heavy interval is representative of the full 600-second render is only partially addressed: deepseek_packet.md:31-33 reports non-overlapping 60-second intervals with correlation 0.740-0.992, but the full per-interval table is not in the supplied evidence.

The learned width control's actual value in the latest run is reported as 0.120 (deepseek_packet.md:39), well below the 0.50 ceiling, so the cap is not the binding constraint; why the optimizer did not push width higher is not established by the supplied lines.
Whether the side path's 16-sample Haas delay (main.rs:5600-5601) contributes to perceived harshness or center bias is not measured in the supplied evidence.
No blinded listening has been performed (context_packet.md:58-60), so perceptual improvement or degradation is not established.
